doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

chapter: Kendrick Lamar and To Pimp a Butterfly
title: Recording Covered at Capitol and jamming with John Mayer
summary: While recording his trio album Covered in L.A., he jammed with John Mayer in the next studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Right. But I’m playing at the Vanguard for a week. But most of the teachers were super cool about that, and the New School was really cool about that. That’s the thing. That’s what you’re there for. You know. So anyway fast forward, I heard “good kid, m.A.A.d city” and it blew me away. And I called Terrace and I was like, “yup, I have to be on the next CD somehow,” to be on Kendrick’s next album. He’s like, “gotcha. We gonna make it happen.” I was like, “aye, bet.” And so fast forward I’m doing my trio album, “Covered” — I put out last year.

My last recording. And I’m in L.A. And that’s the thing about going where the food is, because L.A. is one of those places where there’s a lot of food. So I did two recording nights there. The first night I go, I’m recording at Studio A. I recorded it live in the studio at Capitol Records. In Studio B was John Mayer recording his record. He walks over, he’s like, “hey, Robert.” We’d never met in person. He’s like, “Robert, what’s up?” I go, “hey man, I’ve never met you” blah-blah-blah. He was like, “after you finish your recording, you want to come over to my studio and jam?” I’m like, “aright.” So I finished my recording and I went next door and jammed with John Mayer for two hours. Duo. Just me and him. You know? At the studio on tape.
So I don’t know if anybody will come up with anything, but, that happened. It was like that was pretty awesome.
